A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ToolScope. All 22 pages of v1 and 25 pages of v2, including appendices, equations, tables and figures, are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original tool-selection and retrieval experiments on BFCL, Seal-Tools and UltraTool, alongside ablations and human assessment of documentation quality.

after.justification: V2 retains these experiments and adds functionality-preservation results, human evaluation of merges, merger-model ablations and an end-to-end BFCL experiment.

M1.justification: The core algorithm, pseudocode and standard prompts remain unchanged. However, v2 Appendix M explicitly modifies the merging prompt to rewrite full functionality for executable tools; v1's documented merger produces signatures and docstrings. This is a limited adaptation for the new experiment.

E1.justification: The three original benchmark datasets and selection tasks are retained. V2 adds a limited, 20-query BFCL scenario requiring execution of generated Python functions and correct final answers, extending coverage beyond tool selection.

E2.justification: BM25 and Dense remain the main comparison methods, while DPR and ToolShed remain in the Seal-Tools retrieval comparison. The new end-to-end experiment also uses BM25 and Dense. Alternative merger LLMs are component ablations, not additional competing methods.

E3.justification: Original benchmark settings are retained, but Appendices K–M introduce substantial additional evaluation protocols: functionality-coverage metrics, a rare-capability subset, human assessment of 48 BFCL clusters, controlled merger-model substitutions, and a 20-query executable evaluation using GPT-5 and three human verifiers.

E4.justification: V2 adds analyses of common and rare functionality preservation, human merge correctness, Auto-Correction detection quality, and dependence on the merger LLM. These directly test assumptions that v1's component, threshold, documentation-quality and illustrative case analyses did not establish.

E5.justification: The documentation-rating study retains the same Cohen's kappa, Kendall's tau and p-value reporting in v1 Appendix F.2 and v2 Appendix E.2. New experiments report point estimates without adding repeated-run information, confidence intervals or statistical significance procedures.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark scores remain unchanged, but Tables 9–12 add substantial results: 82–95% tool-call coverage, 80–96% capability coverage, 95.4% merge correctness, 94.4% Auto-Correction F1, and CSR results for alternative merger models. The new end-to-end setting reports 80% accuracy versus BM25's 30% and Dense's 40%; these are new task results, not improvements over v1 under identical conditions.

T1.justification: V2 Appendix K.1 introduces formal definitions of Tool-Call Coverage Rate and Unique Capability Coverage using argument-set inclusion, distinguishing frequency-weighted calls from equally weighted capabilities. Existing method equations are unchanged, and no new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: automated merging with Auto-Correction, hybrid retrieval, reduced context requirements and improved tool-selection accuracy. Added emphasis on scalability reiterates v1's scope, and the headline performance claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 interprets the new evidence as supporting preservation of rare functionality, reliable merging and independence from GPT-4o as the merger. Section 4.2 also cautiously describes downstream gains as preliminary evidence. Existing mechanism explanations, limitations and deployment cautions remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix H.1 adds computational costs, latency and hardware details, while Appendix M documents GPT-5 function generation and the smolagents evaluation setup. Existing hyperparameters and prompts are retained. V1's statement promising code release after legal approval is removed without a replacement access statement.

R1.justification: The bibliography adds references including FAISS, RE-Invoke, Search-R1, WebGPT and smolagents. However, the related-work discussion and positioning of automated merging combined with retrieval remain essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: Changes comprise localized copyediting, a shortened contact-email line, added results paragraphs and appendix sections, and appendix relettering after removal of Code Release. The main narrative and section organization are largely retained.

P2.justification: V2 adds Tables 9–12, repositions existing displays such as Table 3 and Figures 3–5, and adjusts some table formatting. Existing figures and the overall visual design are retained; the revision does not substantially redesign the presentation.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens v1's selection-focused evidence with merge-quality checks, merger-model ablations and an executable BFCL pilot, while documenting computational costs. The improvement is limited: the pilot covers only 20 queries using GPT-5-generated functions, and functionality preservation is measured through argument-schema coverage rather than demonstrated behavioral equivalence. Removing the code-release statement also reduces reproducibility information.
